text: Lesson 6 proved this warehouse was correct once, by running a row-count check by hand. But this warehouse refreshes nightly, unattended — and a one-time manual check can't protect something that runs every single night with nobody watching.

Imagine night forty: a batch of orders lands with a territory ID that doesn't resolve to any dimension row. Nobody is awake at two in the morning to re-run a manual check. By the next day, the executive dashboard, the board deck, and the finance workbook are all quietly under-reporting the same missing orders.

This Python layer is built to catch four real failure modes: row-count mismatches, unexpected nulls, duplicate rows, and orphaned foreign keys — each one a real way this exact warehouse can quietly go wrong, not a vague catch-all.
Next lesson writes the real script — connecting directly to the warehouse in SQL Server and running each of these checks in pandas.
